summary: On Yom Tov we may not trap fish or animals, because trapping is not allowed. But an animal that is already easy to grab may be taken.

chunks.he: אֵין צָדִין דָּגִים מִן הַבֵּיבָרִין בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
chunks.en: We may not catch fish from their ponds on Yom Tov,
chunks.st: One may not trap fish from their ponds on a Festival
chunks.stMore: even with the intention of eating them, as this falls into the category of hunting, a type of labor that is not permitted on a Festival.

chunks.en: and we may not put food in front of them.
chunks.explain: Fish find their own food in the water.
chunks.st: Nor may one place food before them,
chunks.stMore: as it is not his duty to feed them; rather, they maintain themselves by eating smaller fish or different types of algae that grow in the water.

chunks.he: אֲבָל צָדִין חַיָּה וָעוֹף מִן הַבֵּיבָרִין,
chunks.en: But we may catch an animal or a bird from their pens,
chunks.st: However, one may trap an animal or a bird from their enclosures [beivarim],
chunks.stMore: as they are viewed as already captured, and therefore the action is not considered an act of hunting.

chunks.en: and we may put food in front of them.
chunks.st: And one may also place food before them as one does for other household animals.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.en: Not all pens are the same.
chunks.st: Not all enclosures are identical with respect to the halakhot of hunting.

chunks.en: This is the rule:
chunks.st: This is the principle:

chunks.en: Any animal that still needs to be chased and caught is forbidden,
chunks.st: With regard to any animal inside such an enclosure whose trapping is inadequate,
chunks.stMore: meaning that the enclosure is large and contains hiding places so that it is still necessary to pursue and apprehend the animal, it is prohibited for one to catch it;

chunks.en: and any animal that does not need to be chased is allowed.
chunks.st: and with regard to any animal whose trapping is not inadequate,
chunks.stMore: as it is possible to seize it immediately without having to engage in further pursuit, it is permitted for one to catch it.

summary: Traps set before Yom Tov: may we take what is in them on Yom Tov? And a story about Rabban Gamliel and some fish.

chunks.en: Traps for animals, birds and fish
chunks.st: If traps for animals, birds, and fish

chunks.en: that were set before Yom Tov:
chunks.st: were set on the eve of a Festival,

chunks.en: he may not take anything from them on Yom Tov,
chunks.st: one may not take anything from them on the Festival,

chunks.en: unless he knows
chunks.st: unless he knows that

chunks.en: that they were caught before Yom Tov.
chunks.st: the animals found in the traps had already been caught on the eve of the Festival.

chunks.en: Once, a non-Jew
chunks.st: And an incident is related where a certain gentile

chunks.en: brought fish to Rabban Gamliel,
chunks.st: brought fish to Rabban Gamliel,

chunks.en: and he said: They are allowed,
chunks.st: and the latter said: The fish are permitted,

chunks.en: but I do not want to take them from him.
chunks.st: but I do not wish to accept them from him, as I despise him.

summary: When may we shecht an animal on Yom Tov if it is about to die? And how do we carry the meat home?

chunks.en: An animal that is about to die, he may not shecht it on Yom Tov,
chunks.st: If an animal is in danger of dying, in which case its meat would be prohibited as the animal had not been properly slaughtered, and one wishes to slaughter it in the hope that it will be found fit for eating and he will be spared a loss, he may not slaughter it on a Festival

chunks.en: unless there is still time
chunks.st: unless there is still time in the day

chunks.en: in the day to eat an olive's size of it roasted.
chunks.explain: Then we can say he shechted it for Yom Tov.
chunks.st: for him to eat an olive-bulk of roasted meat from the animal,
chunks.stMore: so that it is possible to say that he slaughtered the animal for the sake of the Festival.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says:

chunks.en: Even enough time to eat an olive's size raw, from where it was shechted.
chunks.st: There need not be enough time for him to roast it; rather, it is sufficient even if there is only time to eat an olive-bulk of raw meat from the place where the animal is slaughtered,
chunks.stMore: i.e., from its neck, without going to the trouble of removing its hide and roasting it.

chunks.en: If he shechted it in the field,
chunks.st: If one slaughtered an animal on a Festival in the field,

chunks.en: he may not bring it home on a pole or on two poles,
chunks.st: he may not bring it to his house on a pole or on a set of poles
chunks.stMore: carried by two people, as this appears similar to a weekday activity.

chunks.en: but he brings it in his hand, piece by piece.
chunks.st: Rather, he must alter his usual weekday manner of performing this action and bring it in by hand, limb by limb. A male firstborn of cattle, sheep, or goats belonging to a Jew is sanctified from birth and must be given to a priest to be sacrificed on the altar in the Temple. If a firstborn animal acquired a physical blemish that disqualifies it from being sacrificed as an offering, it still must be given to a priest, but it may be redeemed, slaughtered, and eaten as non-sacred meat.

summary: A bechor animal fell into a pit on Yom Tov. May we take it out and shecht it?

chunks.en: A bechor animal that fell into a pit:
chunks.st: If a firstborn animal fell into a cistern on a Festival, and there is concern that it might die there,

words.note: A firstborn animal. It may be eaten only if it has a mum.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: An expert should go down and look at it.
chunks.st: An expert in these matters goes down into the cistern and examines the animal.

chunks.en: If it has a mum,
chunks.st: If it has a permanent blemish,
chunks.stMore: owing to which it may be slaughtered and eaten,

words.note: A blemish, a mark that makes it unfit for a korban.

chunks.en: he may bring it up and shecht it.
chunks.st: he may raise it from the cistern and slaughter it;

chunks.en: But if not,
chunks.st: but if it does not have a blemish, or if its blemish is temporary,

chunks.en: he may not shecht it.
chunks.st: he may not slaughter it.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.he: כֹּל שֶׁאֵין מוּמוֹ נִכָּר מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם,
chunks.en: Any bechor whose mum was not known before Yom Tov
chunks.st: Even if it has a blemish, it is prohibited to slaughter it, as any firstborn animal whose blemish is not perceptible while it is still day, i.e., on the day before the Festival,

chunks.en: is not ready to be used on Yom Tov.
chunks.st: is not considered to be among the animals prepared prior to the Festival for use on the Festival.

summary: An animal that died on Yom Tov, and challah that became tamei, may not be moved.

chunks.en: An animal that died
chunks.st: With regard to an animal that died,

chunks.en: may not be moved from its place on Yom Tov.
chunks.st: one may not move it from its place on a Festival.

chunks.en: Once they asked Rabbi Tarfon
chunks.st: And such an incident once occurred and they asked Rabbi Tarfon

chunks.en: about this, and about challah that became tamei.
chunks.explain: Tamei challah may not be eaten or used on Yom Tov.
chunks.st: about it. And on that same occasion they also asked him about ḥalla that had been separated from dough and then became ritually impure on a Festival.
chunks.stMore: Such ḥalla is not fit to be eaten by anyone, nor may it be used in any other manner, e.g., as animal feed or as fuel for a fire, on that day.

chunks.en: He went into the beis midrash and asked,
chunks.st: Rabbi Tarfon entered the study hall and inquired
chunks.stMore: about these matters,

chunks.en: and they told him:
chunks.st: and the Sages said to him:

chunks.en: They may not be moved from their place.
chunks.st: One may not move them from their place.

summary: People may share one animal on Yom Tov if they agreed before Yom Tov. We may not use a scale on Yom Tov.

chunks.he: אֵין נִמְנִין עַל הַבְּהֵמָה לְכַתְּחִלָּה בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
chunks.en: We may not sign up to share an animal for the first time on Yom Tov,
chunks.explain: Making a deal like this looks like buying and selling.
chunks.st: One may not register to have a portion of an animal on a Festival ab initio,
chunks.stMore: since it is prohibited to divide up an animal into portions for different people, as this is similar to conducting business, a weekday activity, on a Festival.

chunks.he: אֲבָל נִמְנִין עָלֶיהָ מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב
chunks.en: But we may sign up for it before Yom Tov,
chunks.st: But one may register for the animal on the eve of the Festival,

chunks.en: and then shecht it and divide it between them.
chunks.st: and then those who registered for the animal may slaughter and divide it between them
chunks.stMore: on the Festival itself in accordance with the agreement reached the day before. The next day, each pays the slaughterer according to his portion of the animal.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:
chunks.stMore: A person selling meat on a Festival who wishes to know its weight in order to determine its price may not weigh it against regular weights in the ordinary weekday manner, but he may

chunks.en: A person may weigh meat against a vessel
chunks.st: weigh the meat against a vessel

chunks.en: or against a cleaver.
chunks.st: or against a cleaver [kofitz]
chunks.stMore: and then calculate the weight of the meat by weighing the vessel or cleaver later.

chunks.en: And the Sages say:
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.he: אֵין מַשְׁגִּיחִין בְּכַף מֹאזְנַיִם כָּל עִקָּר:
chunks.en: We may not use a scale at all.
chunks.st: One may not look at the pans of a balance scale at all, meaning that they may not be used for weighing in any manner or for any other purpose.

summary: On Yom Tov we may not sharpen a knife the usual way, and we may not buy meat by price.

chunks.he: אֵין מַשְׁחִיזִין אֶת הַסַּכִּין בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
chunks.en: We may not sharpen a knife on Yom Tov the usual way.
chunks.st: One may not sharpen a knife on a Festival in the ordinary weekday manner.

chunks.en: But he may rub it against another knife.
chunks.st: However, one may do so in an unusual fashion, e.g., to run one knife over another,
chunks.stMore: thereby sharpening the blade.

chunks.en: A person should not say to a butcher on Yom Tov:
chunks.st: A person may not say to a butcher on a Festival:

chunks.en: Weigh me a dinar's worth of meat.
chunks.explain: Talking about money makes it look like weekday business.
chunks.st: Weigh for me a dinar’s worth of meat,
chunks.stMore: since if he mentions a sum of money, it looks like a commercial transaction.

chunks.en: But he may shecht and they divide it among themselves.
chunks.st: But the butcher may slaughter an animal and apportion it among his customers without stipulating a price.

summary: We may not measure things the usual way on Yom Tov. The mishnah tells how Abba Shaul ben Botnis filled his measures before Yom Tov, and how we may ask a storekeeper for eggs and nuts by number.

chunks.en: A person may say to his friend on Yom Tov:
chunks.st: One person may say to another on a Festival:

chunks.en: Fill this vessel for me,
chunks.st: Fill this vessel for me,
chunks.stMore: and I will return its contents or reimburse you after the Festival,

chunks.en: but not with a measuring cup.
chunks.st: but he may not ask him to fill the vessel in a particular measure.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: If it was a measuring cup,
chunks.st: If it was a measuring utensil,

chunks.en: he may not fill it.
chunks.st: he may not fill it.

chunks.en: There was a story with Abba Shaul ben Botnis,
chunks.st: There was an incident involving Abba Shaul ben Botnit, a Sage who was also a grocer,

chunks.he: שֶׁהָיָה מְמַלֵּא מִדּוֹתָיו מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב
chunks.en: who would fill his measures before Yom Tov
chunks.st: who would fill his measures on the eve of a Festival

chunks.en: and give them to his customers on Yom Tov.
chunks.st: and give them to his customers on the Festival.
chunks.stMore: In this way he would know exactly how much he had given each person, without conducting any measurements on the Festival itself.

chunks.en: Abba Shaul says:
chunks.st: Abba Shaul, a Sage distinct from Abba Shaul ben Botnit, says:

chunks.en: He did this even on Chol HaMoed,
chunks.st: He would do this even on the intermediate days of a Festival

chunks.en: so the measures would be exact.
chunks.st: because of the clarity of the measures,
chunks.stMore: i.e., in order to clarify precisely how much must be given to each customer, since the measurement is more precise once the foam of the liquid being measured has subsided.

chunks.en: And the Sages say:
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: He did this even on a weekday,
chunks.st: Even on a weekday it is proper to do so,

chunks.en: so every drop could drip out of the measures.
chunks.st: because of the draining of the measures.
chunks.stMore: This method allows all the liquid to drain fully out of the seller’s measuring utensil so that the amount is exact.

chunks.he: הוֹלֵךְ אָדָם אֵצֶל חֶנְוָנִי הָרָגִיל אֶצְלוֹ,
chunks.en: A person may go to a storekeeper he usually buys from
chunks.st: A person may go on a Festival to a grocer from whom he is accustomed to buy

chunks.en: and say to him:
chunks.st: and say to him:

chunks.en: Give me this many eggs and nuts,
chunks.st: Give me eggs and nuts of such-and-such a number,

chunks.en: because a person usually
chunks.st: as it is the manner of a homeowner

chunks.en: counts them in his own house.
chunks.st: to count this way in his own house. Counting eggs or nuts is not considered a commercial activity, as people regularly mention the number of eggs and nuts that they need.
